disagreements.topic: Recurring 2026 FCF base (agent_1 vs the rest)
disagreements.positions: agents 2-5 adopt round 1's ~$11.7B recurring base ($11B pre-fee guide + $0.73B Brazil) and ~$13.2-13.5B 2027 FCF. agent_1 only partly accepts it: the fee was $2.8B pre-tax (~$2.2B after tax), yet the guide rose only $1.5B, so the ex-fee guide is ~$10.3B. It uses ~$11.3B recurring and $13.0B for 2027.
disagreements.resolution: agent_1's arithmetic point is valid and round 1 overstated the certainty. The Q4'25 letter confirms the $11B guide already included the ~$700M Brazil deposit, which moved from 2025 to 2026. But the Q1 letter says the raise was 'due primarily to' the after-tax fee, which leaves ~$0.5-0.7B of other, unexplained 2026 drag. Some of it is plausibly one-off (WBD deal and bridge costs, and Q2 cash tax on the fee, per the Q2 letter), but that is not disclosed. So recurring 2026 FCF is best stated as ~$11.3-11.7B and 2027 FCF as ~$13.0-13.5B. The gap is worth ~$1/share on a 40%-weighted FCF leg, so it does not move the distribution.
disagreements.evidence: Q4'25 letter: FCF beat its forecast because 'an expected deposit of ~$700M ... with the Brazilian tax authorities shifted from 2025 to 2026. For 2026 ... free cash flow of roughly $11B'. Q1'26 letter: '$2.8B cash receipt' from the fee; 'approximately $12.5B, an increase from our previous projection of $11B due primarily to the after-tax impact'. Q2'26 letter: Q2 FCF 'included higher cash tax payments due in part to the Warner Bros. termination fee'.

disagreements.topic: Timing of the Deutsche Bank upgrade (1-month centring)
disagreements.positions: agent_3 dates the upgrade to Buy ($95 PT) as 2026-09-30 and shifts its 1-month centre up (~$70.8, P(>=70.30) 0.51 -> 0.52). The other agents do not adjust.
disagreements.resolution: The upgrade came out on 2026-09-29. The stock opened at $69.23 and closed at $70.30, up ~2% on the day, so the $70.3 as-of close already prices it. agent_3's extra tilt double-counts the upgrade; the 1-month ladder stays centred at spot.
disagreements.evidence: MarketBeat 2026-09-29: DB upgrade hold -> buy, PT $100 -> $95, stock 'opened at $69.23'; Yahoo/Benzinga: NFLX 'rose 2% Tuesday' (2026-09-29) on the upgrade. Consensus PT ~$95 across 55 ratings (4 Strong Buy, 34 Buy, 15 Hold, 2 Sell).

disagreements.topic: Target multiple and the size of the re-rating (fair values $77-83)
disagreements.positions: P/E legs: agent_3 18x (no re-rate), agents 4/5 19x, agents 1/2 19.5-20x, all on NTM EPS of ~$4.22-4.30 (consensus $4.38 less a 2-4% haircut). agent_5 added a 9-name peer base rate: the median return in the 12 months after an idiosyncratic de-rating of a quality large cap is ~-6%, 4 of 9 positive.
disagreements.resolution: Not resolvable with facts; it is the genuine judgment left. The inputs have converged: every agent now uses the $3.82/$4.56 consensus, 4.08B shares and ~$13-13.5B 2027 FCF, and the fair-value range narrowed from $76-84 to $77-83 (mean $80.3). The peer base rate (small sample, in-lane, from price history) balances the old NFLX-only +90% rebound rate. Together they support the mean's median of ~$76-77, below the ~$80 fair value, rather than a move either way.
disagreements.evidence: Agent files, round 2; Q2'26 10-Q (weighted diluted 4,261.3M vs basic 4,189.3M in Q2).

disagreements.positions: agents 1 and 5 keep $50. They argue a fall to $52 can still come from de-rating alone, since ADBE (2025-26) and PYPL (2022-23) fell ~30% more on multiple compression. agent_4 moves to $51; agents 2 and 3 keep $52.
disagreements.resolution: The peer examples are credible, and at $52 the stock would be ~13.6x 2027 EPS, only ~1.5 turns under the Wells Fargo bear multiple. The reconciled break moves to $51, the forecasters' mean (~13.4x 2027 EPS, ~6.6% FCF yield on ~$13.3B).

disagreements.topic: Net debt used in the FCF leg
disagreements.resolution: The last reported figure is $5.24B at 6/30/26: gross debt $14.36B (incl. issuance costs) less $9.13B of cash and short-term investments. Q3 buybacks running ahead of FCF could raise it, but $6B is an unsupported estimate until the Oct 20 print. The difference is <$0.2/share.
disagreements.evidence: Q2'26 letter, non-GAAP net debt reconciliation: $5,244M.

one_month_reasoning: The Q3'26 print on Oct 20 (guide $12.86B / 33.2% / $0.82, consensus on the guide) is the only scheduled event in the window. The Deutsche Bank upgrade is already in the $70.3 close, so the 1-month ladder stays at the forecasters' mean, centred on spot with ~12% sigma.
confidence_reason: Round 2 converged: agent fair values span $77-83 on shared, verified inputs, and the one outlier (agent_5's P(>=70)=0.67) came back to 0.60. The searches in this round settled only small items: the FCF-base nuance (~$1/share), the upgrade timing already in the close, and net debt. None of them moves the distribution off the mean, so the mean ladders stand.
thesis_break_reason: Below ~$51 (~13.4x 2027 consensus EPS of $3.82, ~6.6% FCF yield on ~$13.3B 2027 FCF, and well under Wells Fargo's $57 bear case at 15x) the market would be pricing estimate cuts, not just de-rating. Examples: a January 2027 guide for high-single-digit growth or margin contraction, Antenna churn clearly above ~2-2.5%, or a large debt-funded acquisition. Lowered from $52 because peer cases (ADBE, PYPL) show pure de-rating can reach ~-26% from spot.
key_drivers: Revenue deceleration: 17.6% -> 16.2% -> 13.4% -> 11.7% guided for Q3'26. The Oct 20 Q4 guide and the January 2027 guide (~10% growth or below) decide the multiple.

Recurring 2026 FCF is ~$11.3-11.7B, excluding the after-tax WBD fee and the ~$0.7B Brazil deposit. That implies ~$13.0-13.5B in 2027, with net debt of $5.24B and $27.1B of buyback capacity shrinking the share count ~3-4% a year from 4.164B.

Engagement versus monetisation: Nielsen share is 7.8% vs YouTube 14.2%, and Wells Fargo sees ~-4% y/y hours per member in H2'26. Antenna churn is still ~2% vs a ~4% industry average, and ads are ~$3B in 2026 with a nearly doubled upfront.

Valuation is ~18.4x 2027 consensus EPS ($3.82) against 2028 at $4.56. The peer base rate says idiosyncratic de-ratings usually do not reverse within 12 months, and the sell-side PT is ~$95 (DB upgrade 9/29 vs Wells Fargo $57 underweight).

fair_value.reason: Unchanged from round 1 and in line with the round-2 mean ($80.3). P/E: NTM EPS at Sep-2027 of 0.25x$3.82 + 0.75x$4.56 = $4.38, less ~3% = $4.25, at 19x = $81. FCF: NTM FCF of ~$14.5B (off a ~$11.3-11.7B recurring 2026 base) at a 4.5% yield, less $5.24B net debt, over ~4.08B diluted shares = ~$77.7. A 60/40 blend gives ~$80.
